title: Conservation of Energy
learning_goal: Apply conservation of energy and the work-energy theorem to analyze energy transformations.

stages.title: 1. Energy changes form
stages.content: Energy can transfer between objects and transform from one form to another, but the total energy of an isolated system remains constant.

stages.title: 2. Mechanical energy
stages.content: When nonconservative effects such as friction are negligible, kinetic and potential energy can trade back and forth while total mechanical energy remains constant.

stages.title: 3. Work-energy theorem
stages.content: The net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy: Wnet = ΔKE.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: A falling object loses 20 J of gravitational potential energy while air resistance is negligible. Its kinetic energy increases by 20 J, so total mechanical energy remains unchanged.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A cart begins with 50 J of potential energy and 10 J of kinetic energy. If total mechanical energy is conserved and the potential energy later becomes 20 J, what is the new kinetic energy?
stages.hint: First find the total mechanical energy at the beginning.
stages.alternate_explanation: Whatever potential energy is lost must appear as kinetic energy if no energy leaves the mechanical system.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, track kinetic and potential energy, apply conservation of mechanical energy, use Wnet = ΔKE, and explain thermal energy changes when friction is present.
